content:
Manchester United completed the signing of Manuel Ugarte for €50m (£42m) plus €10m in bonuses from Paris Saint-Germain on Friday evening, with the Uruguayan promising to “fight for trophies” and help return the club to elite level.

The 23-year-old signed a five-year contract with the option of a further 12 months, becoming Erik ten Hag’s fifth major acquisition of the window. Ugarte gives the manager another senior No 6 to pair with Casemiro, adding depth and steel to United’s midfield options.

Ugarte said: “It is an incredible feeling to join a club of this magnitude – one that is admired all around the world. The project that the football leadership discussed with me is extremely exciting. Manchester United is an ambitious club and I am an ambitious player. I know how incredible United fans are and I cannot wait to experience Old Trafford. I’m someone who is so determined to succeed. I will sacrifice and give everything for my teammates. Together we will fight to win trophies and reach the level where this club needs to be.”

Dan Ashworth, United’s sporting director, said: “Signing Manuel was another of our primary targets for this summer. He fits the profile we were looking for — young, robust, and with a clear will to improve. He brings defensive coverage and the ability to recycle possession under pressure, which will be vital across a long season.”

Sources close to the discussions revealed United moved quickly after identifying midfield reinforcement as a priority following a busy scouting process. The deal marks a significant investment in the squad’s spine and signals the club’s intent to compete on multiple fronts next season.

Supporters greeted the arrival with optimism, hoping Ugarte’s combative style and work rate will complement the creative talents already at Old Trafford. Ten Hag now has greater flexibility to rotate and to protect his more advanced operators, while also preparing for the demands of domestic and continental schedules.

Ugarte’s arrival closes another chapter of summer recruitment for United but also raises expectations. The next challenge for the club will be to integrate him smoothly into the setup so that on-field cohesion improves quickly and results follow.

Any other questions?
